Do my parents have dementia?

I keep noticing ‘weird’ behavior. Asking about basic card game rules they’ve know for years. Confusing a text with a call. Cooking with obvious spoiled cheese/meat. Not being able to use the self-checkout. Not being nice to the neighbors. Not being able to see emotions in other people. Delusions and overal apathy. I could go on and on.

I’m in a bit of a pickle since they aren’t willing to go to the doctor. 

I would like to know what you first notice about your parents/husband/wife/loved ones that makes you think something’s wrong.  
I would really like to know the stories that made you seek for a diagnosis.

How to start conversation with father and siblings about elder care

I'd like to start a conversation with my father and siblings about elder care, so we can plan for the future. There is a lot for us to consider and unpack and a lot of decisions that need to be made in order for us to plan for our father's care in his retirement years. He is 77 years old, still healthy and alert. But dementia runs in his family and I know his physical and mental health may decline. I'd like me and my siblings to talk and plan so we know our roles and what to do when and if that happens. 

Issues I'd like to us to talk about include:

1) Power of attorney. Establishing it while he is still healthy in case he gets incapacitated. We need one or more of us to have the power of attorney to make decisions and interact with government and financial entities on our father's behalf.

2) If my father and brother would consider simplifying their housing arrangement. Right now, my sister and I live and work in the US. My father and brother live in Asia. This makes planning and logistics complicated. What makes logistics even more complicated is my father and brother live in a big, 3-story house that my father and mother built from their retirement savings when she was still living. It is a huge property with a big garden that takes a full-time housekeeper to keep clean, a part-time gardener, and a lot of maintenance to keep things in shape. I'd like my father and brother to consider simplifying things starting with selling the house and property and to consider moving to a smaller place like a 2-bedroom house or condo. Something that does not require a lot of upkeep to keep clean and manage.

3) Our aunt -- our late mother's sister -- lives in the same house with them. Our late mother invited her to live with them when she was living and continues to stay in the house. She is elderly also but has her own adult children. She has lived in the house with them for the past ten years rent-free. I'd like for my brother and father to consider having her move out to live with her own children. My reason is that taking care of one elderly person is a big responsibility for my brother primarily and indirectly for my sister and I from overseas. Having to be responsible for the care of two senior citizens is a bigger responsibility and I do not want us to be responsible for our aunt, given she has her own adult children. Being responsible for our father is a big enough responsibility for the three of us. 

How best to start the conversation? I feel like I will be introducing awkward topics such as letting go of the house and property which has a lot of sentimental value to the family, and also the issue of having our aunt move out to live with her own children. I appreciate any tips and advice.

Can my brother and I both be caregivers?

My father had a stroke last March and after going through all the hoops and red tape I became his caregiver in February. It’s not easy but as a family we’re working daily to make sure we can give adequate care. My brother is a contract worker and his contract ended and his availability is much more open now. I appreciate his help immensely and it’s greatly needed as my mother travels for work. Soon my brother will have to pick up another contract to keep up with his bills. I am already getting paid to be my father’s caregiver during the day, but this is a 24/7 situation. Is it possible for me to stay his caregiver and for my brother to be his night time caregiver and get paid? Mentally and physically I need more help. I quit my job but I can’t expect him to do the same and still be able to take care of himself. Is there an option we can use?

I feel like I lost custody of my mom tonight.

Mom (dementia) had a bad episode where I was the lightning rod catching all of her paranoid thoughts (none of them true, I have been careful and respectful). She occasionally talks of unaliving herself and she claims (falsely) that's what I want. It's definitely not. 

Background: i know she wants to drive and have her independence again. So I take her grocery shopping and on weekend trips to the mountains. Anyway I try. I'm not perfect, I'm not s medical professional, but I know my mom the best, and I'm her only child. We've always been very close. 

Tonight: I was advised to take her you the ER because this episode could be caused by a UTI or other infection. (All tests negative) now I have MDPOA and they judged her not competent to go home alone. But since she said she didn't feel safe they are keeping her and referring her to caseworker and social worker and they will "call me" tomorrow.  

I have this sinking feeling they will force a care home and I will have no say, and neither will she.

Feeling trapped

I feel trapped by my emotions about caring for my elderly parents. I'm their legal and medical POA. At first, I told myself it was a privilege to care for them bc they worked hard so I could go to college. But now I'm overwhelmed handling all their finances, legal matters, house maintenance, etc. Whenever I think, when will it all end? or what a relief it will be when this is all over, I feel miserable bc I know it will only end one day once they're dead, buried, and I sell their house, finalize their finances, and send out the last of their death certificates.

I really don't like it when my mom starts being suspicious

So my mom went to AL in August. It's been a mixed bag, she stopped falling and has been more social, but she is just a difficult CONTROLLING person. I think these settings are really hard for control freaks which she is. 

We have spend a lot of time there this month and did a lot of things she wanted, and she has been a little happier. 

Tonight she called me, she decided one of the waiters is pouring syrup on her fish. In retaliation for going to dinner late. 

This just sounds nuts. Maybe they are not thrilled she rolls in late-- but I can't imagine a world where a waiter finds a bottle of syrup and pours it on her food. 

She has an old bathrobe that went missing and turned up. She thinks the aid stole this and was told to give it back. This thing is from the 70's. 

I have a lot of issues with my mom, she was emotionally abusive to me growing up, but one of her saving graces is that in general she is a fairly kind and positive person to most people. 

I have to be honest. I despise this side of her. I really hate it.I feel like she is almost projecting the fact that she has trouble with her temper. In what world does a tired frustrated waiter go an find a bottle of syrup and put it on her food. Plus old people love syrup. I told her that since she was eating at desert time maybe someones desert like fruit cup spilled on her plate OR there was a sweet lemon glaze on the fish, which is not something we are accustomed to. 

But I just feel like if I put the work into getting things going well there she is going to come up with delusional conspiracies like this-- or maybe it's just the dementia.

A Birthday Rant

I made the mistake of getting my mom technology for her birthday.

  
My parents watch television through a laptop, logged into their streaming providers connected to their television.  I got them a Roku so they can access their streaming directly thru the remote.  

I cheerfully told them I'd be at their house to install it at noon.

At 11:30a, I get a call from my mom.  My parents are screaming at each other about how the other is setting it up wrong, my dad doesnt want "them" to have access to hear their conversations, that they don't want to give "them" their information or credit card.  I sit on the phone dumbfounded.  Speaking is futile.  They are screaming at each other.

  
It felt like my childhood all over again.

  
I just hung up and texted that I was returning the roku.  Happy Birthday, mom.

My dad gets paranoid when I go on vacation

I am, for all intents and purposes, the only person in my dad’s life. He lives in a retirement community. My sister-in-law will help out with his care if I am away.

My dad is prone to bouts of paranoia when he has manic episodes. I am noticing a pattern that when I am going to be away with my family, this paranoia seems to get triggered. He lives in a supportive environment where all meals are provided, his laundry and room cleaning is done for him, his medication is administered by nursing staff and there is a doctor on call who can visit you right in your room. If ever there was an emergency, my sister-in-law would step in or staff would call an ambulance. So when I am away, he is perfectly safe and cared for. But something about me being away seems to trigger anxious feelings that become paranoid accusations. 

 I went away in March and my dad became paranoid that I was lying about where I was and also that I had cleaned out all his money. He even called his financial advisors during my absence to check if his money was still there (it was, of course). 

This weekend I am away with my family and my dad has called me three times very upset that I have “locked him out of his accounts” and he can’t make any more Amazon purchases. The nurses from his retirement home also emailed me to say he came down to report to them about the bank accounts and was considering calling the police. 

I understand he doesn’t choose to be paranoid and that it must be a scary and vulnerable feeling. The truth about his finances is that he has a credit card with a low monthly limit because he spends impulsively online. I just paid the credit card bill at the beginning of the month and he has already maxed it out again. When he is lucid, he’s concerned about money, but when he’s manic he can’t seem to keep track of his spending at all. 

He can’t listen to reason when he’s like this, but I’ve had to reiterate several times that this is not an emergency, that I am on vacation with my family and it will have to wait. I have a difficult relationship with my dad already and it makes me so frustrated and upset that I’m rewarded for my efforts in caring for him by being accused of stealing and threatened with police intervention.

My elderly parents have a foster child and my dad keeps force-feeding her carbs and sugar to an extent that it has caused her to be diagnosed with pre-diabetes 

I am in my thirties and looking for advice on what to do. He himself is a type 2 diabetic and he keeps saying "well I can't eat this but she can!". 

This is solely my dad's doing. When I was growing up under their care, I was NEVER allowed to eat sugar or other junk food and I didn't even know what soda tastes like. It seems that this shift in my dad's mental state might be due to senility? He has been acting very strange in recent years and overly hostile/aggressive for no reason and acting like he takes personal offense to things that don't have anything to do with him! It's really hard. 


As a daughter who doesn't live with them, what can I do? Should I try to speak with their case worker?

Mom dragging her feet going to assisted living

For the past month, I have been care taking my Parkinsonian mother after her release from the hospital for failure to thrive and malnutrition. To do this, I have had to quit my nursing job and temporarily relocate to her home to care for her ahead of transitioning her to assisted living. Problem is, she is very reluctant to go to AL. She has 3 cats and because of these animals I understand that giving up animals that give you comfort is very traumatic and not a small issue at all, which is why I elected to bring her home to spend time with her cats ahead of her going to a care facility. But my Mom cannot take care of herself, and she will always need some form of help to accomplish her ADL's (despite getting much stronger and better fed under my care). However she has become very reluctant to make the decision on which AL place to relocate to. She also seems unconcerned that her care is impinging on my life, and acts that my care will be long-term, despite my making clear that this was only a short-term situation. In short, it feels selfish and manipulative, and her concern seems to be more with her animals rather than the upheaval that this is causing in my life, and the sacrifice I've made.

Feeling lost

I don’t know how I ended up here.  I’m feeling lost and no one to talk to.  I’m a 45 year old female.  I have a husband that travels 5 days a week for work and have an extremely challenging 8 year old son with ADHD and severe deregulation.   I work full time a super intense job.  I’m also the primary responsible party for my parents even though I have 2 siblings.  My father has Parkinson’s and Vascular dementia.    My mom had been taking care of my dad (with me assisting) until it became too much for her and so in September we moved my dad to a Memory Care facility.  We thought it would take the load off of us but he didn’t transition well. The facility has the most wonderful care but Dad was miserable not being home.  He’d cry everyday all day.  He’d complain.  And we even considered moving him back home but the reality was that he was falling constantly and we couldn’t get him up without a firefighter.  He was up all night and sometimes trying to escape.  I would be awake days at a time trying to care for him.  It was unrealistic we could take care of him.  I was already resentful.  Frustrated sad.  I was spending thousands of dollars of my money that should have been my retirement and son’s college money.  My son needed me and I was absent.  My husband complaining that I was dead all the time.  I have spent years sacrificing my life for dad.  Then 2 weeks ago he got pneumonia and he hasn’t recovered.  We moved him from hospital to hospice care 8 days ago.  I just left hospice and we said our last goodbyes to him. He hasn’t woken up in days.  Now that he’s gone I feel so sad. Lost.  Regretful.  I hate myself for complaining and feeling resentment. I’m sad. I don’t know what to do with myself. Now I have a funeral to plan and I can’t function.  See here I am still up can’t sleep and talking to the public bc I have no one to talk to or understands the war I’ve been through.

Is it dementia or something else?

My mother is in her early 70s and for the past 15 years has been behaving increasingly oddly. There is a whole history with this and it has been extremely shocking to go through. 

She will frequently say things that are inappropriate and has no filter, but when she's around her friends and family members, she seems to be able to seem normal. She is extremely liberal and into all of the No Kings and BLM stuff but recently said something horrific to a Black person (that wasn't exactly racism towards him but just not something anyone should say out loud). 

I ended up up having to cut ties with her because I deal with health issues and she was ignoring my health boundaries to the point where I was ending up in the ER and putting me in multiple situations that were extremely dangerous for me to be in. She doesn't seem to have any self reflection and she is in complete denial of every cruel thing she has ever done to me and dealing with it has been extremely confusing. I yelled at her for putting me in the situation that almost killed me and she acted like I was the one in the wrong and like I owed her a major apology when she was the one that almost got me killed. 

Before 15 years ago, she wasn't a bad mom. She was a normal person, I think. I fully believe she used to be a very nice person. Then she started putting me in extremely evil and abusive situations out of nowhere and becoming extremely immature. Dealing with her now is like dealing with a kid, and it has been a difficult dynamic because I am expected to treat my mother with the same patience as a mother should treat her child. 

She gets angry after spending time with people if I try to talk to her at all and will start yelling at me saying she doesn't want to talk to me, even when we were on completely good terms and I wonder if it could be from "showtiming" and how it just takes people a lot of energy to seem "normal" when they have diminished capacities.

 Dementia does run in the family and I have always wondered if this could be what has been happening. It has been difficult because she has refused to get checked out for 15 years and has become increasingly cruel and cold over the years, recently to the point where she did put me in a situation I could have died in with no remorse, which was very scary for me.

  
She is incapable of having more than an extremely surface level relationship with anyone and I don't think she used to be that way before all the weird behavior started 15 years ago. 

  
If this sounds like dementia, how would I get her checked out by a doctor? For those who have dealt with family members with early onset dementia, does this seem like something that could be in line with that?

Pons Stroke

My (fairly young - just turned 56) mother just had her second stroke a few months ago. Her first was mild, but this one was severe. It came a few months after a two week ICU stay because she didn’t tell anyone she wasn’t taking her insulin for a year (she was ICU bound because her glucose was over 600 and hypertension was also through the roof, she also went into septic shock and renal failure).

This second stroke was deemed a Pons stroke. She’s extremely stubborn but stayed in the hospital for a week or two, and thankfully agreed to go to inpatient rehab for five weeks after. 

I could tell, even with all that “help,” she needed so much more adamant help, in terms of regaining her dominant hand and foot and mouth and speech, so I begged her to continue to do outpatient after inpatient was no longer covered. She said she “felt fine” and refused it. She genuinely made immense progress the entire duration, and her voice sounded normal again just after leaving inpatient. I saw her for the first time in 4-5 weeks yesterday and it’s plain as day on her face (more than it was then) that she suffered a stroke. Her speech is so slurred now, it sounds like the very fucking day she first had it. Mind you, she sounded exactly normal like herself every day I called her every week prior. I can’t understand her now. 

I don’t understand. I don’t know what to do. I tried to do all the research, I’ve tried to guide her and my father, but my mother isn’t even 60, and she sounds and looks like someone far older who suffered a “major” stroke. She is, to my knowledge, taking her Monjauro, and seeing her doctors. 

I’m remiss, and I guess mostly probably just venting. I wish I’d joined this sub after her first stroke. 

What can I do? Or she do? Is there any hope, all this time later?

Fall Alert Device Recommendations

Hi guys. I lost my father in October and now my mom has had to move out of her home and is now living in a small room at her best friend’s house out in the boondocks in Missouri. She couldn’t live there alone. She’s having to sell all her belongings. 😢 Sadly, I’m stuck across the country and cannot move to be closer and cannot move her here. She can’t do stairs and I live in a small upstairs apartment. She also needs a walk-in shower and we don’t have one.  

Anyway, her friend is 17 years younger than her (my mom is 87 with memory issues and mobility issues) and will be going to work full time after the first of the year. My mom needs a fall alert medical device. I’ve been researching and so many seem like scams. Ideally, I could get her one that she can wear like a watch and that could alert authorities if she falls and is unable to alert anyone (such as becoming unconscious).  

Anyone have recommendations? I wish we could put her in assisted living, but Medicare doesn’t cover that and we can’t afford it. (She doesn’t have Medicaid.) Medicare won’t cover home assistance like an aide, nor will it cover anything toward housing of any sort with the exception of 30 days of acute care.

Bad Dreams?

Not the person(s) you care for, but you? 

My spouse of 40+ years was DX'd with Parkinson's nearly 11 years ago; he's fairly late-stage, ambulatory with a walker but uses a wheelchair 85% of the time, needs help with all ADL.
